chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from al-Mithammi, from Aban, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who hired an animal from another man to go to a specific place, and he went beyond that place to which he had hired it, and the animal died, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is liable (for the value), and upon him is the hire proportional to that (distance traveled).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a hired animal dies after traveling beyond the agreed destination?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *daman* (liability) in rental contracts, ruling that the hirer bears the risk of loss once the agreed term or destination is exceeded. This establishes a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for determining proportional compensation (*kari bi-qadr*) when the utility of the hired item is consumed beyond the agreed scope, reflecting the broader Islamic legal emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions.
